summaries.Good news: Today's uplifting stories celebrate human resilience and scientific breakthroughs—from a 99-year-old wing-walker defying age to Stanford researchers reversing coral bleaching in record time, reminding us that recovery and adventure are always possible.
summaries.Ideas: The day's ideas explore practical challenges and ethical boundaries in our digital world, from AI liability and encryption threats to smarter ways we're choosing to live online.
summaries.Technology: Today's tech advances span energy optimization, sustainable design, and AI-powered tools that tackle real problems—from grid power efficiency to repairable electronics and adaptive defense systems.
summaries.Design: Today's design stories showcase how architects and designers are transforming spaces through resourcefulness and reimagination—converting industrial relics into cultural landmarks, repurposing materials into homes, and rethinking everyday objects with intention.

items.title: Coral Bleaching Reversed at Record Speed Using New Stanford Method: ‘Not a Lost Cause, at All’
items.snippet: Coral bleaching has been reversed at record speed using a new method developed at Stanford University. items.line: Stanford researchers have achieved the fastest documented coral bleaching recovery ever—ghostly white corals restored to full health in just seven weeks—proving restoration is achievable at scale.
